change_request.title: PERF: read SAS page headers in Cython instead of Python
change_request.author: jbrockmendel

task.task: Improve SAS7BDAT reading performance by parsing page headers and dispatching page types in Cython instead of Python.
subtasks: Extract `_read_page_data()` from the Python reader’s `_read_next_page()` to handle page I/O, pointer reset, EOF detection, and incomplete-page validation while retaining the Python metadata-reading path.
Add an initialized, bounds-checked Cython `read_uint16` helper using `memcpy` and byte swapping, and parse page type, block count, and subheader count directly from the cached page buffer.

Update Cython page iteration to process metadata pages through `_process_page_metadata()`, accept data and mixed pages, skip unsupported page types, and clear the cached pointer at EOF. Synchronize the initial page after Python metadata parsing.
Keep string decoding in the Python result-construction path rather than Cython, preserving text conversion and inferred string dtype behavior.
Add a pandas 3.1.0 performance release note referencing #47339 in the appropriate sorted position, and run `pytest pandas/tests/io/sas/` to verify compatibility.

change_request.title: BUG: Timedelta kwargs fall back to coarser resolution on overflow
change_request.author: jbrockmendel

task.task: Fix Timedelta keyword construction to fall back to an exact coarser resolution when nanosecond int64 bounds overflow, while preserving existing non-overflow behavior.
subtasks: In pandas/_libs/tslibs/timedeltas.pyx, compute total nanoseconds once and attempt nanosecond construction first. Only on OverflowError, select an exact resolution using divisibility by 1,000, 1,000,000, and 1,000,000,000 to choose ns, us, ms, or s without losing precision.

If construction at the selected resolution still overflows, raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta with the existing component-based diagnostic. Preserve the normal-path microsecond conversion and explicit nanoseconds keyword behavior.

Update constructor tests to cover large days and minutes values that now succeed, microsecond and millisecond fallback units, preserved nanosecond behavior, and truly out-of-bounds values such as days=10**15. Run the timedelta scalar tests.
Add a pandas 3.1.0 release note describing the keyword-constructor overflow fix and referencing issue #46587.

subtasks: Rename _astype_float_to_int_nansafe to astype_float_to_int_nansafe and update its existing caller so NumpyExtensionArray can reuse it.

Document the conversion bug fix in the pandas 3.1.0 release notes, referencing issue #41724.
